instrument_name: SC Revenue Ruling #22-3 Employer Wage Withholding Requirements (income tax)
article_or_section: Summary of Employer SC Wage Withholding Requirements; Examples 1-7
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident employee: SC withholding applies wherever the work is done, except no SC withholding on a resident working outside SC when the wages are subject to the other state's withholding laws and the employer withholds for that state (12-8-520(C)(1)); if the other state has no income tax (example Florida) 100 percent is withheld for SC. Nonresident employee: only wages for services rendered in SC, apportioned by the share of the payroll period worked in SC (example 70/30); a nonresident working exclusively outside SC is not subject to SC withholding even if the employer is in SC (Texas professor example): no convenience-of-the-employer rule. Exceptions: wages expected under 1,000 USD; nonresident wages not above the IRC 151(d) personal exemption amount (not for construction/installation/engineering work with SC situs) per 12-8-520(D)(3); waiver 12-8-1040; military spouse exemption (RR21-10). The one-half rule (117-910.1) does not apply to partly-in-SC nonresident wages. An employer outside SC with an employee earning income in SC must withhold (12-8-510).
